newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Sierra Leone talks resume in Ivory Coast.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone talks resume in Ivory Coast.

text.p: West African foreign ministers began a second day of talks with envoys of Sierra Leone's military rulers on Friday as part of efforts to reverse a May 25 coup there and restore President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah to power.
The talks in Ivory Coast's commercial capital adjourned on Thursday on a hopeful note with Nigeria's foreign minister, Tom Ikimi, saying they had made substantial progress.
Nigeria, which heads a West African force trying to restore peace and democracy to both Sierra Leone and neighbouring Liberia, has spearheaded efforts to return Kabbah to power.
Sierra Leone's neighbours decided in Guinea on June 26 to pursue dialogue and economic sanctions to try to persuade the junta to reinstate him, but they retained a military option.

Ivory Coast, Nigeria, Ghana and Guinea were given the job of holding talks with the junta and reporting back to Nigeria's military ruler, General Sani Abacha, current chairman of the Economic Community of West African States.

"We feel we have made substantial progress and that the atmosphere exists for a substantial breakthrough," Ikimi said after Thursday's talks. He held separate talks with members of the junta's delegation before Friday's session, witnesses said.
Liberia holds national elections on Saturday to end seven years of civil war and officials said that Ikimi and the other foreign ministers planned to be there.
"Peace in Liberia will not be long-lasting if there is not peace in Sierra Leone," Tom Ikimi told the meeting on Thursday.
Nigerian soldiers have clashed with Sierra Leone troops and their rebel allies on several occasions since Nigerian gunboats bombarded the capital in a June 2 show of force.
